hard_failures: The answer key twice states that the Class A mean of 66.67 lies above ten of the twelve scores, but it lies above only seven (52, 55, 58, 60, 62, 64, and 66). This is a repeated factual error in the worked explanation and model synthesis.
incorrect_or_ambiguous_items: Items 3 and 10 repeat the false claim that ten of twelve Class A scores are below the mean; the correct count is seven.
errors: The answer key makes a repeated seven-versus-ten count error in explanations used to interpret skew and choose a summary statistic.
critical_observations: Independently recomputed every center, spread, quartile, histogram count, and probability; the requested numerical answers are otherwise correct.
The false count is not needed to establish right skew—the mean is above the median and 96 is an outlier—but it remains an explicit factual claim presented as evidence in two worked explanations.
artifact_findings: Exactly ten readable worksheet problems were visually confirmed.
The strict hard gate treats a false repeated statement in the explanatory answer key as an internal mathematical inconsistency even when the principal requested values are correct.
rationale: Re-audit under the strict gate changes this verdict from ACCEPT to REJECT: the key twice gives a demonstrably false count as explanatory evidence, so the artifact is not fully mathematically correct or internally consistent.
